articles.title: X suspends 13,000 accounts linked to Iran, China and Russia 'targeting US politics'
articles.summary:
X suspends 13,000 accounts linked to Iran, China and Russia 'targeting US politics'

Social media platform X says it has recently identified and suspended more than 13,000 accounts involved in three suspected foreign influence operations, linked to Iran, Russia and China, that targeted US “political conversation”.

The company did not specify how many accounts were linked to each of the three countries.

In a post on the platform, X’s Global Government Affairs said the networks “used inauthentic accounts to post and amplify content about US politics, targeting candidates and public figures across the political spectrum”.

X said its Safety team uses a variety of detection methods to proactively find and act on activity that breaks its rules, as the platform prepares for the upcoming 2026 US midterms. The company said its Authenticity Policy is central to this work, whether the target is spam networks or entities engaged in influence operations.

People come to X to talk about what's happening in the world, including the upcoming 2026 US midterms. Free speech is the bedrock of a functioning democracy, and we are proud that X is the global town square where these debates happen. Our job is to keep that conversation authentic, open, and safe. To ensure these fundamental values are protected during elections, our Safety team uses a variety of detection methods to proactively find and act on activity that breaks the X Rules. These measures build on the safety protections we run 24/7, year-round. X's Authenticity Policy is particularly important to this work. Whether it is spam networks or entities engaged in influence operations, we are actively working to identify and stop coordinated inauthentic behavior that undermines the integrity of our platform.  Through proactive sweeps and investigations, X recently identified and suspended more than 13,000 accounts involved in three suspected foreign influence operations linked to Iran, Russia, and China that targeted US political conversation. The networks used inauthentic accounts to post and amplify content about US politics, targeting candidates and public figures across the political spectrum.  X's Civic Integrity policy addresses misleading content that could affect participation in elections or other civic processes. This includes content that may confuse people about how, when, or where to participate, or that aims to discourage participation. X relies on Community Notes, which let people add context and credible sources, alongside platform moderation. Users can report content under "Civic Integrity" in our in-app reporting flow, and their submission will be routed to request a Community Note, a collaborative way to add helpful context to posts and keep people better informed. Additionally, in critical escalations, X may apply a Civic Integrity label to posts that violate our policy. We remain committed to X as a global town square where people openly debate topics of public interest and engage with election-related information. Our work continues through Election Day and beyond. See our Civic Integrity Policy for more information: https://t.co/FJFuvEC9RE

— Global Government Affairs (@GlobalAffairs) October 14, 2026

articles.title: Trump again: 'Iran lost all its defences, war will end soon, fuel prices drop'
articles.summary:
Trump again: 'Iran lost all its defences, war will end soon, fuel prices drop'

US President Donald Trump has reiterated that the war on Iran will end “very soon”, while claiming Washington was in "total control" of the Strait of Hormuz.

Speaking at a rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, Trump said Iran had lost its navy, air force, radar systems, and air defences.

“Their first level leaders are gone. They picked a second level. Their second level leaders have gone. They picked the third level. Half of them are gone, they made me promise not to take out anymore. And I did. I promised them. he said.

“So I probably went a little too far. I’m sorry, because I don’t know who the hell we’re dealing with anymore.”

Trump said the conflict had pushed up fuel prices, but will drop "very soon" when the war ends.

articles.title: US employees 'need' special authorisation to use Saudi airports
articles.summary:
US employees 'need' special authorisation to use Saudi airports

The United States embassy in Saudi Arabia has said US government employees require special authorisation from Chief of Mission to use any airport in the kingdom following recent Houthi missile and drone attacks.

In a security alert, the embassy urged US citizens to follow alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence via cellular broadcast, while warning them of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations and other travel disruptions.

It urged US citizens to exercise “extreme caution” when using Saudi airports and to check flight statuses directly with airlines.

Saudi Arabia: U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom. Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh through October 17. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport. More at https://t.co/40vTFgJuRu

— TravelGov (@TravelGov) October 14, 2026
